_doc: QA environment description, read by .claude/lib/qa-probe.sh (which /prime-qa injects at command load). STARTER DEFAULT: `base_url` and `local_url` are empty, so the probe reports 'not configured' and /prime-qa still loads the QA context — it just cannot resolve a BASE_URL. Fill this in per project. Nothing here is secret: it is hosts and commands, never credentials. Credentials stay in .env, which the probe only stats (size + mtime), never reads.
_base_url_doc: Candidate DEPLOYED host QA verifies against, no trailing slash. Empty => skip deployed probing and go straight to local.
_probe_paths_doc: Paths appended to base_url that must ALL be reachable for the deployed host to be chosen. Name the routes QA actually needs (the app entry point, a component workbench, an API health route) — not just '/', or a half-deployed host reads as healthy.
_local_url_doc: Local fallback root, used when the deployed host is unreachable or a probe path fails. Empty => no fallback, and the probe says so instead of inventing one.
_local_serve_command_doc: How a QA session starts the app itself when it falls back to local. Printed for the tester; the probe never runs it.
_local_serve_command_alt_port_doc: Same, for a SECOND concurrent QA session — the first already holds the default port. Leave empty if parallel local sessions are not a thing here.
_local_serve_command_tier1_doc: Non-browser apps only (see qa-evidence-families.md §2 tiers). How to start the app in the OTHER tier than local_serve_command — typically inspection-only, without the driver extension that Tier 2 needs but that mocks the device keyboard. Empty => the app has a single way to run.
_build_sha_url_doc: Optional URL returning the DEPLOYED build's commit SHA (a build-info endpoint, or an HTML page carrying <meta name="build-sha">). Used to detect a deployed build lagging local HEAD. Empty => the probe stamps 'skew not verified' rather than fabricating an endpoint — an unverified skew must never read as a verified match.
_artifacts_dir_doc: Where QA persists screenshots / traces. Must be gitignored — QA evidence is point-in-time, not repo history. The probe warns if it is not.
_env_file_doc: Credentials file whose PRESENCE (never contents) is part of the preflight.
_browser_mcp_process_pattern_doc: pgrep pattern counting browser-automation MCP servers already running on this machine — information about parallel QA sessions, not a gate.
_mcp_config_file_doc: MCP config checked for the flag that makes concurrent browser sessions safe.
_parallel_safe_flag_doc: The flag that isolates each browser session's profile (Playwright MCP: --isolated). Without it a second concurrent QA session collides with the first.
_component_mount_url_template_doc: How ONE component is reached for observation by the runtime-UI verifier. Placeholders: {BASE_URL}, {id}, {route}. Component workbench => '{BASE_URL}/storybook?path=/story/{id}'; plain app route => '{BASE_URL}/{route}'; custom harness => whatever mounts one component in isolation. EMPTY => dormant: qa-runtime-ui returns NEEDS-HUMAN for every criterion instead of guessing a URL. A project with no component mount point is a normal state, not a misconfiguration.
_touch_sweep_widths_doc: Widths the cross-device verifier (qa-runtime-device) sweeps on a TOUCH device profile — one per touch-plausible tier, taken at the tier's lower edge where its min-width query first fires (e.g. [360, 390, 768]). Empty => the device lane has no tiers to sweep and its rows route to NEEDS-HUMAN.
_pointer_sweep_widths_doc: Widths the desktop lane (qa-runtime-ui, /gates:design-quality-check) sweeps with a fine pointer — one per pointer tier, lower edge (e.g. [1024, 1440, 1920]). Never overlap with touch_sweep_widths: a touch device at a desktop width is a configuration no user has.
_breakpoint_token_prefix_doc: CSS custom-property prefix of the project's breakpoint tokens (e.g. '--bp-'). The device verifier reads every '<prefix>*' via getComputedStyle(document.documentElement) and cross-checks it against the token source named in CLAUDE.md — a mismatch means stale compiled CSS, and every tier reading would be wrong. Empty => the cross-check is skipped and said so.
_device_mcp_server_doc: Name of the device-mode browser MCP server in .mcp.json (the one started with a mobile/touch profile, separate from the desktop browser server). Empty => family `cross-device / viewport` routes to NEEDS-HUMAN; the desktop server is never used as a stand-in.
